newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to allow 10 groups to open Cuba news offices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to allow 10 groups to open Cuba news offices.

text.p: The United States government will announce on Wednesday that it will grant licenses to 10 organizations to open news gathering offices in Cuba, informed U.S. sources told Reuters.

One informed source said the Clinton administration would grant the licenses to CNN, CBS, ABC, Dow Jones, the Associated Press, the Chicago Tribune, the Chicago Sun-Times, the Miami Herald, the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies, and Los Angeles-based Spanish-language television network Univision.

President Bill Clinton announced in October 1995 that he would allow U.S. news organisations to open offices in Havana for the first time in more than three decades in an effort to promote direct contacts between the United States and the Cuban people.
About a dozen news organisations applied for licenses, but a formal decision was delayed by the February 1996 shooting down of two Florida-based civilian aircraft by the Cuban Airforce.
Officials at CBS, CNN and ABC said they had not heard of the decision. Miami Herald Foreign Editor Maria Garcia said she had had no official word. "I hope so, but I haven't heard that yet," she said.
